newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar authorities fear toxic dumping in ocean.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar authorities fear toxic dumping in ocean.

text.p: Port officials at Manakara, southeastern Madagascar, say thousands of fish in nearby waters of the Indian Ocean appear to have been killed by toxic substances dumped in the sea.
Radio Madagascar on Saturday quoted Martial Rakamisilahy, Manakara port deputy, as saying he had no doubt the fish had been poisoned.
Rakamisilahy said the air in the port town had a sickening odour.
He appealed for disaster aid, and said it was feared people may have collected some of the dead fish and eaten them.
For the present, no poisoning cases had been reported in the area, he said. But warnings had been circulated in coastal areas against eating fish found dead.
In 1993, 100 people in the area died after eating shark meat. Smaller numbers of deaths were reported in 1994 and 1995 from the same cause.
Madagascar authorities are haunted by fears of possible illegal toxic dumping in the waters surrounding the island republic's 5,000 km (3,000 mile) coastline, government officials said on Sunday.

During the recent presidential election campaign former president Albert Zafy -- who was narrowly defeated in the poll -- alleged that he had been offered millions of dollars to allow toxic products to be dumped in Madagascar waters, but had rejected the offer.
